Security in one place: who signs in, what each one may do, and the defenses at the edge (CORS, security headers, CSRF). An entity marked @security(principal) is a realm of its own, with its own sign-up, sign-in and sessions: User and Customer never share an identity. Identities live apart from the entities, in the security_ tables, with the principal's id: passwords (Argon2id), Google and GitHub sign-in, sessions in cookies, short JWTs with /.well-known/jwks.json, email verification and password reset. Each entity says who may list, read, create, update or delete it. Without a principal, it only sends the security headers and answers CORS.

```esquadro
blueprint security
```

## Works with

- **Requires** [app](../app/), [env](../env/), [http](../http/): the app must use them too.
- **Works with** [mail](../mail/), [domain](../domain/), [postgres](../postgres/), [migrations](../migrations/), [jobs](../jobs/), [worker](../worker/), [rest](../rest/), [api_docs](../api_docs/), [i18n](../i18n/), [observability](../observability/), [testcontainers](../testcontainers/), [compose](../compose/), [docker](../docker/) when the app uses them.

## Options

| Option | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | `"/identity"` | The prefix of the identity routes: /identity/&lt;realm>/sign-in. |
| `services` | list | `[]` | The roles of service keys, for what is no person (a system, a script, a partner): the rules name them as service.&lt;role>, e.g. @security(read [user.admin, service.reader]). An admin creates a key with &lt;app> security key create &lt;name> --role &lt;role>; it goes in Authorization: Bearer sk_... |
| `hsts` | bool | `false` | Send Strict-Transport-Security, behind HTTPS only. &lt;APP>_HSTS overrides it. |
| `public_url` | string | `"http://localhost:8080"` | The address of the app, for the links of emails and the OAuth callbacks. |
| `redirect_urls` | list | `[]` | Where the app may send people back to after sign-in or an email link. |
| `session_days` | int | `7` | Days a session lasts without being used to renew it. |
| `session_idle_hours` | int | `24` | Hours of inactivity that end a session. |
| `session_max_days` | int | `30` | Days after which a session ends, used or not. |
| `session_ip` | bool | `true` | Keep the address and the browser of each session. |
| `session_user_agent` | bool | `true` |  |
| `token_minutes` | int | `15` | Minutes a JWT lasts. |
| `rotate_keys_days` | int | `0` | Days between rotations of the JWT signing key, checked every hour by jobs or the worker; 0 is never. |
| `verify_email_hours` | int | `24` | Hours an email verification link works, and minutes a password reset link does. |
| `password_reset_minutes` | int | `60` |  |
| `password_min` | int | `12` | The shortest password. NIST asks for 15 when the password is the only factor. |
| `password_max` | int | `128` |  |
| `password_blocklist` | name | `"none"` | none, lists (the passwords of password_lists, and those made of a sequence, a repetition, the app's name or the person's email) or pwned (all that, and Pwned Passwords). |
| `password_lists` | list | `[]` | Files of passwords to refuse, one per line, read when the app starts (relative to where it runs): lists for the language and the country of its users. |
| `pwned_fail` | name | `"open"` | open or closed: whether a password may be set when Pwned Passwords does not answer. |
| `argon2_memory_kib` | int | `19456` | Argon2id's cost; OWASP's minimum by default. |
| `argon2_iterations` | int | `2` |  |
| `argon2_parallelism` | int | `1` |  |
| `pepper` | bool | `false` | HMAC every password hash with SECURITY_PEPPER, kept out of the database. Changing the pepper means resetting every password. |
| `lockout_attempts` | int | `5` | Failed sign-ins before an account is locked, and for how long; never in development. |
| `lockout_minutes` | int | `15` |  |

```esquadro
blueprint security {
  path "/identity"
}
```

## Environment variables

Read when the app starts; see [Environment variables](/esquadro/language/environment/).

| Variable | Type | Value | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SECURITY_SECRET` | string, secret, required outside development | generated in development | Signs CSRF tokens and encrypts the JWT signing keys; esquadro generates one for development. |
| `SECURITY_PEPPER` | string, secret, required outside development | - | With the pepper option, the key every password hash is mixed with; kept out of the database. Changing it means resetting every password. |
| `<APP>_HSTS` | bool | the hsts option | Send Strict-Transport-Security, behind HTTPS only. |
| `SECURITY_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` | string, required outside development | - | The OAuth client of the app at Google (console.cloud.google.com, APIs & Services, Credentials), for the realms that sign in with Google; its redirect URI is &lt;public_url>&lt;path>/&lt;realm>/oauth/google/callback. |
| `SECURITY_GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` | string, secret, required outside development | - |  |
| `SECURITY_GITHUB_CLIENT_ID` | string, required outside development | - | The OAuth app at GitHub (Settings, Developer settings, OAuth Apps), for the realms that sign in with GitHub; its callback URL is &lt;public_url>&lt;path>/&lt;realm>/oauth/github/callback. |
| `SECURITY_GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET` | string, secret, required outside development | - |  |

## Annotations

| Where | Key | Type | |
|---|---|---|---|
| entity | `principal` | bool | The entity signs in: a realm named after it. |
| entity | `signup` | name | open (anyone signs up), invite or closed (the default: only by the app's security command). |
| entity | `providers` | list | password (the default), google and github. |
| entity | `roles` | list | The roles of the realm. |
| entity | `permissions` | list | The realm's own permissions, besides those of the entities, e.g. [orders.refund]; roles get them with grants. |
| entity | `grants` | list | Which roles have which of those permissions, as role.permission, e.g. [admin.orders.refund, staff.reports.view]. |
| entity | `verify_email` | name | required, optional (the default) or off. |
| entity | `password_reset` | bool | Whether a forgotten password can be reset by email (the default). |
| entity | `password_min` | int |  |
| entity | `password_max` | int |  |
| entity | `password_blocklist` | name |  |
| entity | `lockout_attempts` | int |  |
| entity | `lockout_minutes` | int |  |
| entity | `list` | list | Who may list, read, create, update or delete the entity: public, a realm (whoever signed in to it), realm.role, or owner (the principal the record belongs to); write is create, update and delete. |
| entity | `read` | list |  |
| entity | `create` | list |  |
| entity | `update` | list |  |
| entity | `delete` | list |  |
| entity | `write` | list |  |
| entity | `owner` | name | The relation to the principal a record belongs to, for the owner rule, when the entity has more than one; a principal owns itself. |

An annotation is written `@security(key value)` on the element.
